# How the record grew, commit by commit

Four files are measured at every first-parent commit of `main`, from the first commit under `explorations/` (`446836590`, 2026-08-19) to `HEAD` when `measure.py` runs: in the data here, to `de6e51170` (2026-11-05), 3,462 commits:

- the gap ledger, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`: characters and rows;
- `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`, `POSITIONS.md` and `INDEX.md`: characters.

A row of the ledger is a table line that starts `| N |` above the heading `## Revival worklist`. Characters are Unicode code points. Bytes are in the CSV beside them.

## What the chart shows

`record-growth.png`, titled "Growth of the record, 09-08 to" the last commit's day: three panels on one time axis (the ledger's characters, its rows, and FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX in characters, labelled with the revival page's names for them, the facts, the decisions and the index), and a vertical line through all three at each batch's landing, with no batch names. Since 2026-11-23 `chart.py` ta

- The ledger went from 83 rows (39.6K characters, 09-09) to 638 rows (1.25M) by batch 10 on 10-03. Its first 309 rows (326K) came before the first climb; to batch 10 the 20 landings, with their run windows, added 16 rows and 46K characters each on average.
- On 10-08 the ledger was rewritten (`ae4f8e38a`, 14:06 UTC). The 638 rows kept their numbers, stand in fifteen topic sections and are cut to 1,200 characters at most. The file fell from 1,246,580 to 540,693 characters in that one commit (-706K, 57%), and the mean row from 1,863 to 832 characters (365 rows had been over 1,200; the longest was 12,075). The earlier text of every changed row, and the
- So "rows almost never shrink" held to 10-03 (after entry they gained 308K characters and lost 0.8K, `../gap-ledger-archaeology.md` section 1.1) and holds no longer. Since the rewrite, the commit that closes the rows a batch fixed shortens them (status FIXED) and moves their earlier lines to the history file: -7.3K, -6.7K and -2.4K for batches 11, 12 and 13 (the history file gained 18K, 15K and 7
- Batches 11, 12 and 13 landed on 10-09 (04:05, 14:39 and 23:03 UTC), after 5.5 days with no batch (10-03 10:58 to 10-08 23:42). From batch 10's landing to batch 13's the ledger gained 55 rows and 56K characters (the growth of its commits, not the cuts of the closes), 18 rows and 19K for each landing, against 16 rows and 46K to batch 10. It was 694 rows and 581K characters at `c8258deda`, a mean o
- From the ladder climb's start (09-17 06:01) to batch 13's landing (10-09 23:03), the batch run windows are 28% of the clock (151 of 545 hours) and hold 89% of the characters the ledger gained (868K of 978K) and 93% of its new rows (356 of 384). They hold 17% of INDEX's growth and 19% of POSITIONS'. To batch 10's landing (10-03 10:58) the shares were 35% of the clock (135 of 389 hours), 88%, 92%,
- FACTS grew to 352K at batch 7b (09-30), then lost 92K in one commit on 10-02 (the rung entries cut to the fact), after a 55K rewrite on 09-20 and 44K on 09-30. It was 294K at `c8258deda`: 250K on the morning of 10-08, 257K when batch 11 started, 294K at batch 13's landing. The two commits "FACTS consolidated before climb batch 12 and 13" changed it by +2.2K and +0.2K. POSITIONS peaked at 105K (0
- From 10-03 11:36 to batch 11's start (10-08 23:42) the ledger gained 2 rows, and FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX gained 12K, 17K and 26K: commits about process, skills and the record, and batch 11's preparation. From batch 11's start to batch 13's landing they gained 37K, 5K and 13K.
- On 10-13 FACTS went from 257.6K to 90.2K characters and POSITIONS from 103.5K to 33.9K, together 361.1K to 124.1K (-237K), from `12df81e7e`, the commit before the consolidation's first chunk `55f1a1352` (18:16 UTC), to `b67abe3d2` (20:13). The chunks (`55f1a1352` to `ab933086b`) cut 160.6K and the removal of the entries that moved to the skills (`1632b5dfa`, `9dd34a1f2`, `b67abe3d2`) 76.4K, 49 m

## Files

Scripts, run from the repository root:

- `measure.py`: reads the four files at every first-parent commit with `git cat-file`, writes `series.csv`, `changes.csv`, `by-day.csv`, `top-additions.csv` and `per-batch.csv`, all five at each run. About 11 seconds at 3,462 commits. Needs `git` and Python 3.
- `classify.py`: who made a commit (coordinator, a worker, a batch's gather, a consolidation), by subject, paths and time, for `measure.py`.
- `chart.py`: draws `record-growth.png` (1800 by 2640 pixels, 300 dpi, 6 inches wide, its smallest text 14 pt) from `series.csv` and `landings.csv`; it reads no git. About 1.5 seconds. Needs `matplotlib`.

Regenerate: `python3 explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-growth/measure.py`, then `python3 explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-growth/chart.py`. At a landing, `explorations/coordinator/tools/revival-page/update.py` adds the landing's row to `landings.csv` if it is missing, then runs the two (its README).

Data (input, kept by hand):

- `landings.csv`: the 37 batches (batches 14 to 22 added on 2026-10-24 and 22c to 25 on 2026-11-05, each run start from its first agent's first line in the run's transcripts, its landing the gate's tables commit, its code commits the first table of `climb-batch-N/RECORD.md`; a row that `update.py` adds takes its run start from `--run-start`, and its note says which), the run's start (UTC), the lan
- `labels-2026-10-02.csv`: the class of each commit as the earlier worker labelled it on 2026-10-02 (regexes and hand corrections), kept as data.

Data (output of `measure.py`):

- `series.csv`: one row for each of the 3,462 first-parent commits (to `de6e51170`): time, commit, the ledger's rows and characters, the characters and bytes of the four files, the batch whose landing it is.
- `changes.csv`: one row for each commit and file that changed the file (1,422 rows, 9 of them side-branch commits). Size, change in characters and bytes, class, batch, how many entries it added or lengthened and the three largest. A merge keeps its net change; the four side-branch commits it brought in have kind `branch_commit`.
- `by-day.csv`: characters added and removed for each file, UTC day and class.
- `top-additions.csv`: the ten largest single-commit additions of each file.
- `per-batch.csv`: the four sizes at each landing, and the change since the previous landing.

The earlier measure, carried over because the new chart does not hold it:

- `boot-size.csv`, `boot-size.png` and `boot-size-chart.py`: the size of the coordinator's boot (K tokens) at nine compactions, 09-19 to 09-30, from the session transcripts, with the sizes of FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX then. Not extended: the transcripts are not in the repository.

## Method and limits

- Every git read is bounded by a range or a count. `measure.py` runs `git log --first-parent` twice over `446836590^..HEAD` (the commits, then their paths with `-m --name-only`), one `git cat-file --batch-check` and one `git cat-file --batch` for all the blobs, a `git log` over each merge's side branch (its first parent to its second) for each file, `git log -1` and `git diff-tree` of each side-br
- The line is `git log --first-parent` of `main`. A merge's net change is one step. The ledger's first commits were made on side branches, so on the line it first appears at 09-09 00:30 with 83 rows.
- Landing marks are the 37 commits of `landings.csv`; batches 13b and 15b, which landed outside a batch run, have none. A batch's run window is its start to its landing. Starts are to the minute, so a commit in the launch minute but before the launch counts inside the window (`12ce5b201`, 20 seconds before batch 13's launch: +1.7K of INDEX; without it INDEX's share of the windows is 16%, not 17%).
- The share of the ledger's characters in the windows counts the characters it gained: the sum of the commits' positive steps. To batch 10 that equals its net change (88.4% either way). After the rewrite the net change says nothing of the batches, so only this sum is used. For INDEX and POSITIONS the shares are of the net change, as before.
- A class after 10-02 comes from `classify.py`'s regexes with no hand check, so it can be wrong. Sizes and rows are exact.
- `classify.py` was extended for batches 11 to 13 in two places, and nowhere else. Their commits of the same kind as the earlier batches' were labelled otherwise: (1) the gather's "Close the rows climb batch N fixed" was "probe/judgement worker (during a batch)" and is now "batch rung/gather worker", as the gather's other commits are (new pattern `GATHER`); (2) the INDEX lines of a batch's review 
- The ledger rewrite and the closes move text to `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger-history.md`, which is not measured: the ledger file is, so the chart's fall of 10-08 is text that moved, not text that was lost.

# Session transcripts — Fortress revival

This is an **orphan branch** (no shared history with `main`) holding the raw
Claude Code session transcripts of the Fortress modernization work, kept for
later analysis of the engineering and debugging practices used. It never
merges into `main`; the large JSONL blobs live only in this branch's history.

## Layout

```
projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl        main session transcript
projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl.parts/  the same, cut at line
    000.jsonl, 001.jsonl, ...                     boundaries into 64 MiB parts
                                                  once it outgrows GitHub's
                                                  100 MiB blob limit;
                                                  `cat *.parts/*.jsonl` rejoins
projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>/subagents/   delegated-agent transcripts
    agent-<id>.jsonl                              each subagent's own transcript
    agent-<id>.meta.json                          prompt, timing, token counts
reports/probe-and-pin.html                        worked example: a narrated
                                                  debugging report generated
                                                  from this very transcript
reports/HOWTO.md                                  how to generate more reports
                                                  in that style
scripts/backup_transcripts.py                     snapshot + redaction filter
scripts/backup.sh                                 unattended commit-and-push
                                                  wrapper (Stop-hook friendly)
```

The project slug is the working directory with `/` → `-`

Questions 3 to 5 move a sentence; they do not lose it. Four habits put in an entry what belongs elsewhere: the lab notebook (how it was found), the changelog (what changed), the citation reflex (a line number on each claim) and the cache (a copy of another entry). One habit cuts too much: bare numbers and codes. "With the diff it has 14" tells nothing until it says 14 of what.

**A count that each landing changes**, such as the distance to the switch-over, has one entry: the current value, what it counts, the kinds that lead, and how to read a move. The batch's commit stage rewrites the value at each landing. Other entries give that entry's number, not the value. The counts by kind stay in the file that the gate writes. A count from one measurement is not kept current: its entry says so, and keeps the parts that a decision reads.

**The size.** About 240 entries stay, and the goal of about 145K characters for both files allows about 600 each. So 600 is a check, not a cap. An entry may pass it when the questions keep a sentence that needs the room. Its writer names, in the chunk's report, the decision or the misreading that the sentence prevents, and shorter entries pay for it: a chunk's total stays under 600 characters times its entries. The record test checks the result: no worse than 27 of 30.

**The register** is halfway to ASD-STE100: one statement per sentence, active voice, short sentences, one word for one thing. Use no shorthand that a reader new to the project cannot follow. Say what every number counts.

- reported each record edit to him.

**Why.** The boot read held two instructions that conflict: the knowledge base's "entries are never deleted; a superseded entry gets 'superseded by …' appended" (2026-09-15) and Pavol's reason for the 09-24 gardening, that the boot files hold "a clean current state". - The boot read stays full-context. The peace of mind of a coordinator that knows the project without him is worth the tokens, and no size target applies.
- The protocol becomes a few principles and a short list of hard rules, led by: follow the purpose, not the wording; keep effort and record in proportion, so a side remark changes behaviour and not the record; notice what is going wrong and propose the fix before he has to. This is `record-keeping-proposal.md`, Appendix A, and the knowledge base's README is Appendix B. Both replaced the old files on 2026-09-27 (`9e7d12c75`), together with the five sentences the proposal moves into the manuals.

12:4. **Searching the record.** An exchange is one message of yours and all that the coordinator does until your next one. Fable 5.2 searched FACTS, POSITIONS or INDEX in 33 of 100 exchanges. Opus 5.5: 31. Fable 5.1: 16. So it does not search less. In 4 of the night's 7 corrections that a search would have settled, it had searched, in the wrong place or not far enough. A count of searches cannot see that.
14:6. **The light boot has a price.** Corrections that a search would have settled came 19 times in 398 of your messages when FACTS and POSITIONS had not been read whole since the compaction. They came 2 times in 202 when they had.
17:9. **The boot's cost.** A full boot reads 1.1M bytes and adds about 430K tokens: FACTS 145K, INDEX 134K, the held list 45K, POSITIONS 41K. On 10-14 the same files were 0.4M bytes. A light boot adds 60K to 90K. After a full boot you sent a median of 8 messages before the next compaction. After a light boot, 17.
30:- **A boot** is counted at each compaction. The stretch from one compaction to the next is an **interval**. A boot is **full** if FACTS and POSITIONS were read before the boot ended, and **light** if not. The boot ends at his first message, or a worker's notice, after its fifth tool call.
60:**Counts** (`searches.py`; 689 exchanges since 10-22 22:56, when the light boot's rule came: Fable 5.1 400, Opus 5.5 161, Fable 5.2 128). A search is a tool call of the coordinator's own on FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX or their histories.
63:- When FACTS and POSITIONS had not been read whole since the compaction, where the light boot's rule asks for a search before every statement: Fable 5.2 48% of 56 exchanges, Opus 5.5 38% of 53, Fable 5.1 17% of 299.
90:- By what was in context: corrections of kinds 1, 2 and 7 came 19 times in 398 messages when FACTS and POSITIONS had not been read whole since the compaction (4.8 per 100) and 2 times in 202 when they had (1.0). By model: Fable 5.1 10 in 299 against 1 in 101; Fable 5.2 7 in 55 against 0 in 72; Opus 5.5 2 in 44 against 1 in 29.
101:- **"The summary carried the earlier loads of the parts as done": not so.** The summary (`C:13842`, 28K characters) names two parts as files, `batch.md` and `delegating.md`, and has one line on the earlier boot: "a full boot was done (FACTS, POSITIONS, INDEX whole; PLAN's head; boot note; held list; delegating part; his profile)". The interval before (the full boot of 11-15 19:43, `C:13164`) had loaded only `delegating.md` and `batch.md`. There were no earlier loads of `record.md`, `road.md`
172:- Measured over every whole-file read of FACTS, POSITIONS and INDEX in the boots: 24M characters cost 8.3M tokens, 2.89 characters a token.
173:- The steps today, in bytes and tokens: FACTS 363K bytes, 126K tokens by size and 145K as measured at 12:29 with its line numbers; INDEX 366K, 127K, measured 134K; the held list 138K, 48K, measured 45K; POSITIONS 116K, 40K, measured 41K; the two cores by the Skill tool 63K, measured 21K; the boot note 27K, 9K; `batch.md` 15K, 5K; `delegating.md` 12K, 4K; his profile 9K, 3K; PLAN's first section 11K, 4K. All steps: 1,120K bytes, 388K tokens by size.
174:- Growth of what the steps read: 409K bytes on 10-14, 651K on 10-23, 769K on 11-01, 939K on 11-08, 1,120K on 11-16. FACTS went from 95K to 363K, INDEX from 206K to 366K, POSITIONS from 35K to 116K, the held list from 10K to 138K.
182:**What it cannot show.** What each file in context is worth. Section 3 gives one number for it: corrections of kinds 1, 2 and 7 at 4.8 per 100 of his messages without FACTS and POSITIONS whole, against 1.0 with them.
190:1. **A hook that names the part at the first act of its kind after a compaction.** It would fire before the first edit of FACTS, POSITIONS or INDEX (`record.md`), the first Agent or Workflow call (`delegating.md`), the first batch workflow or batch brief (`batch.md`), the first edit of PLAN or the review queue (`road.md`), and, if wanted, the first commit, the first check-in armed and the first read of a transcript. It fires only if the part has not been read since the compaction.

===== 31848 2026-11-24T07:33:03.003Z
Both workers are back. The order of declarations still decides in five places. Two of them are your call. The other three are mine (last item), and none changes what a program runs. The nine steps are in the review: https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/blob/main/explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-36/tie-rule-review.md

**Fork 1: a tie at a type that holds no value**
```
trait A excludes B end
f[\T extends A\](x: T): ZZ32 = 1
f[\T extends B\](x: T): String = "b"
g[\X extends { A, B }\](x: X): ZZ32 = f(x)
```
- No value is both an `A` and a `B`, so `g` can never run. The checker must still type `f(x)`.
- Today `g` compiles if A's `f` comes first in the file and fails if B's comes first. Through an api, it's always "Ambiguous call".
- 1a. A static error, "Ambiguous call", everywhere. This is the specification's sentence, the team's later papers, and Java's, C#'s and Swift's way.
- 1b. Type the call by the intersection of the two return types. This is sound, since no value reaches it, and close to Julia's way.
- 1c. Refuse `X extends { A, B }` itself, as a type with no values. No team text states this rule.
- I recommend **1a**: it was the planned rule, and it needs no new one.

**Fork 2: what a compiled call dispatches over**
- Two apis declare `choose(s: S)`, and `choose(t: T)` with `choose(v: V)`. `V` lies below both `S` and `T`.
- With `s: S = Vo`, walk runs `choose(v: V)`, the most specific, as it should. Compiled code runs the body at `S`: it dispatches only within the component of the declaration it names.
- Where a `comprises` clause ties two declarations, which body runs depends on which file name sorts first.
- 2a. The compiled call dispatches over every visible declaration of the name, whichever component declares it. Then neither the order nor the named declaration matters. This is what walk does, and what the designers wrote: the static step is only an optimisation of dynamic dispatch. It costs a code-generator rung, not measured.
- 2b. A static error where a more specific declaration lies in another component. This refuses programs that walk and the specification run.
- 2c. Name one declaration, picked by a stated rule. The order no longer decides, but `choose(s)` still runs the wrong body.
- I recommend **2a**: it is the designers' rule and walk's behaviour.

**Mine, without a decision of yours:**
- A tie among conversions is decided by a rule or refused, never by the JVM's hash order. Today it changes only which conversion method the code names, not what runs.
- Two imports of one signature are refused as duplicates. Today they crash the code generator.
- The error reported follows the decided declaration, not the first in the file.

`record-clarity.js` rewrites record entries so that a reader who knows the language, but never saw the conversation or the batch behind an entry, can tell what it says. Ask of each sentence, and act on the answer:

1. Would the reader do otherwise without it? Keep it.
2. Would the reader misread another sentence without it? Keep it.
3. Does it tell how the fact came about: a date, a batch, a correction? Move it to the history.
4. Is it detail needed only while doing the work: a line number, a list of sites, a timing? Leave it in the report, and name the section.

## Reading and writing

- `git log -S'F-87' --oneline -- explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md` lists the commits that touched an entry.
- To read a history in depth, or a report's passage, send a Sonnet scout. The provenance lines tell it where to dig.
- `record.py`'s header gives its usage. `add`, `set`, `merge`, `remove` and `apply` write; each needs `--from PATH#HEADING` or `--note WHY`. The tool stamps the time and copies the earlier line to the history.
- Before every commit, run `record.py check --base <the commit before your edits>`. It shows that nothing was lost, and reports each entry over 600 characters.
- Commit the record file and its history together.
- Write a decision into POSITIONS in the next commit after the curator states it. A proposal of yours enters only at the curator's yes.
- The record is public and names models on purpose. Hold nothing back from it for that.

## The pass

Run the pass when a worker finishes, and before the next boot or batch reads FACTS. In a batch, the commit stage runs it, with this part quoted in its prompt. After a lone worker, you run it.

The pass owns each entry's final wording. A rung writes its findings as draft entries: the claim, its conditions, its evidence and what it means.

1. Write each new fact as an entry, or rewrite in place the entry that it changes. A rung writes its entries in a file `record.md` in its worktree, and the gather folds them in with `record.py apply`.
2. Give each change its provenance: the report section, the commit, and why.
3. Check each entry against its source, with bounded `grep`s:
   - The cited report section holds what the entry left out.
   - The entry keeps the source's scope: the path (walk or the compiled path), the call form (a dotted method call against a top-level call), the range of values and the conditions. Ask: does the entry let a reader conclude more than the evidence shows?
   - If a behaviour changed, grep FACTS for it, linked or not. Each entry that states it is updated, or says how it differs.
4. Cut any plan or status from each entry (above). If the cut text named a PLAN item or a review-queue item, check that the item names the entry.
5. Report each entry over 600 characters, with the question that keeps its extra sentence.

Run the same pass on POSITIONS at each landing, and when the curator replaces a decision.

## A consolidation

A consolidation runs the pass over whole sections. After a batch lands, the record-landing workflow consolidates its entries (`references/batch.md`, "The landing").

A dead end is a store that takes items in and has no working way to let them out.

8. **The held list.** It holds 80K characters and is read at every boot. A line leaves only at a trim.
   - Fix: each line names its exit when it is written: a decision in POSITIONS, a task for the skill writer, or an answer in chat. The line leaves when that happens.

9. **Stores that only cost tokens.** The skill's `sources.md` (357K) is larger than the skill. FACTS (403K) is read whole after a boot. PLAN's "Where we stand" is 15K in five bullets.

One finding would change a decision of yours: P-180's scope (finding 4). Four fixes change how you and the coordinator work, and wait for your yes: 1 (with 5), 2, 3 and 8. The rest are the coordinator's.

## The common cause

The record-landing workflow (`explorations/coordinator/tools/record-landing/`) runs after every landing with "no step of yours between" (`coordinator/references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 4). It is the inflow of five stores at once:

- the review queue and PLAN's review list, by its routing writer (`routing.md`, "A queue item": "Each item for the curator that no file holds becomes one");
- the `fortress-repo` skill, by its skill task and the orientation update;
- the page of `fortress-repo` changes, one item for each skill change;
- FACTS, PLAN's "Where we stand", INDEX.

Each of these stores has an exit that needs the curator: a queue item leaves "only with his word on that same item" (`routing.md`, "A move to (a)"); a page item "stays until the curator says ... that they have read it" (`skill-rewrite.md`, step 7). So the inflow is automatic and runs at the machine's speed, and the exit is manual and runs at one message a time on a phone. No rule sets a size at which the inflow stops.
**The other stores** (`git cat-file -s COMMIT:PATH` on 11-05 and on 11-23): PLAN 203K to 325K, of which "Off the path, parked" is 225K and 484 lines, with 37 lists "listed for his review"; FACTS 290K to 403K (253 to 326 entries, so 1.2K an entry against the 600-character check); the held list 57K, 129K on 11-16 before a trim, 81K now; the boot note 18K, rewritten in 1,008 commits. The workflow's rule that makes a trap a skill sentence (dead end 4).** `record-landing/skill-task.md`, step 2: "If the data names a trap or a wall of a row that the part has no sentence for, and a worker who follows the part would fall into it, add one sentence where the part keeps its traps." Nothing in the planner's brief reads the ledger for rows to fix: a row gets a rung only if the post-batch review's list "for the batch after" or a PLAN line names it, and the inventory found PLAN lines that leave a row "with the next rung that edits" a file, which names no rung. **Fix:** (1) delete that sentence of `skill-task.md`; a worker already lists the rows that cite a file before it edits the file (`fortress-repo`, "Rules for every task"), so the ledger is the home of traps and the skill is not. (2) The planner's brief gains one step: `ledger.py find --open --cites FILE` for each file a rung names, into the rung's section. (3) `ledger.py close N` prints each skill line that names row N, and `landing-check` fails while a closed row is named in the skill; this gives a skill passage its exit. (4) A `CONTESTED` row (29 to 40 in 18 days) is a question for him kept outside the queue: `landing-check` reports a `CONTESTED` row that no queue item names. This carries out P-180 and needs no word beyond A1.

**C2. Sorts and reviews that end as a file (dead end 6).** The learning file of 11-05 (117 items, no page, one commit); the coordinator's work file (53 items, 17 marked skipped, no commit since 11-05); the dockets of 11-10 and 11-15 (the second's 99 closable and 6 stale items still owed in the boot note); the curator's profile, read after every boot and last changed on 10-16. Retire the two dockets and the work file into the triage now running. Update the profile from his page comments, or stop reading it.

No step consumes either. **Fix:** owed work moves to one housekeeping list (the work file's form), and the record-landing workflow gains a last stage, or the coordinator launches one Opus worker at each landing, that does every line it can and reports the rest. A line that outlives two landings is done or dropped. His question of 08:4x today, "Can you plan a batch for such housekeeping chores?", is the go for the first one.

**C4. Stores that only cost tokens (dead end 9).** `sources.md` gets a line for each skill change and is read by nobody whole; the commit message can hold the same provenance, and `git log -S` finds it. Keep it only for a rule that comes from the curator's words. FACTS is read whole at the first landing after a boot (about 140K tokens); read what the landing changed, and query the rest. PLAN's "Where we stand" grows a clause at each landing; have the routing writer rewrite it whole within a stated size. ## A consolidation

A consolidation runs the pass over whole sections. Run it on FACTS before each batch launches, since the batch's workers read it.

- Make a chunk of each section, 20 to 32 entries.
- For each chunk, a Sonnet scout gathers each entry's report sections, its commits and the curator's dated words.
- An Opus writer reads this part, the chunk and the scout's file, and writes an apply file. It runs `apply` and `check --base` in its own worktree.
- You apply each file on `main`, run `check --base`, commit and push.
- Check the result with a small quiz on the records at hand, without the curator: decisions stay as good, and a reader follows the pointers when needed. If something critical is lost, restore it entry by entry.
